_README: Optional config for the Wildcard Vehicle Generator.
Rename to 'wildcards.config.json' (drop the .example) to activate it.
Delete it any time -- every setting has a built-in default, and with no
config at all the program behaves exactly as it does out of the box.
YOU DO NOT NEED THIS FILE TO ADD OR REMOVE WILDCARD LISTS.
Slots are the .txt files themselves: drop a new one into the wildcards
folder and it becomes a slot; delete one and it goes away. Slot order is
a plain sort on the filename, which is why they are named a1, a2, a3,
b1... -- the prefix is what puts them in order. The part after the first
space is just the label shown in the GUI.
Inside a list: one entry per line, and every entry ends in '__'.
The '__' is a SPACE, not a separator -- entries are glued together and
then every '__' becomes a space. That trailing '__' is what keeps the
spacing right when the next slot is switched off, so do not drop it.
Lines starting with '#' are ignored, so you can comment or park entries.
_default_slots: Which slots are switched on when the program starts.
Default: a2, a3, c3 -- a vehicle, a connector and a gun noun.
Unknown keys are ignored; if none match, every slot starts on.
_civilian_slots: Which slots the 'Unarmed civilian' button leaves switched on.
Default: every slot whose name starts with 'a', except the connector.
Set this if you add slots and want to say exactly what a civilian
vehicle is made of. Unknown keys are ignored.
_connector_slot: The slot holding the joining words ('with a', 'mounting a'...).
Default: 'a3'. Only used when 'civilian_slots' is absent -- it is the
easy way to keep the default rule after renaming the connector list.
Remove the 'civilian_slots' line above to see this take effect.
_list_dirs: Where to look for the .txt lists, relative to the program folder.
Default: the 'wildcards' folder beside the executable. Set this only if
you keep your lists somewhere else. Multiple folders are merged and
sorted together, so a slot's folder does not affect its position --
